transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I'm mostly here because my wife and my director at work thought it might be a good idea to just check in. I've been really, really driven lately—which is normally a good thing, right? You kind of need that in IT management. But I guess I just can't seem to stop launching new projects. 

I've been drawing up all these new work plans, setting up pretty aggressive certification schedules for myself, totally overhauling our home network, messaging a bunch of old contacts... just staying highly productive, really. But, um, I guess I sort of blow past normal limits sometimes? It gets a bit intense, I suppose, to the point where my wife or my boss has to actually step in and tell me to slow down. 

I hope I'm explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to do by being here.
Have you ever felt so energetic or worked so intensely that you were unable to function at your job or had to be hospitalized because of it?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I was unable to function, exactly. It's just that, well, sometimes my enthusiasm gets a little ahead of the practicalities? Like, there was this one server migration at work that... didn't go quite as planned. I was just trying to get it done faster, you know? But it caused some issues, and they ended up putting me on administrative leave for a bit. Just to let things cool down, I think. I hope that makes sense?

And at home... well, my wife has had to help me manage things a little more lately. Like, she's had to kind of step in with our finances because I got a bit carried away buying equipment for the home network. And she reminds me to stop working so late, which is good of her. We do end up arguing sometimes when I'm just so focused on my ideas and she wants me to slow down... I really don't mean to be difficult, I just get so wrapped up in it. 

I guess I've also sort of stepped back from some other things, too. I used to be really involved with the music at our church, and I liked rock climbing and mentoring junior staff, but... I just haven't been able to be as reliable with those lately. I keep meaning to show up, but my mind is just on all these other projects. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Aside from these periods where you feel driven and energetic, have you ever experienced times where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lacked interest in almost everything for a period of two weeks or more?

Um, well... I guess I have had times like that, yes. I mean, everyone gets down sometimes, right? But, um, there are these stretches where I'll wake up and just feel... I don't know, like a failed version of myself? 

It's just this heavy, flat feeling. And it gets to the point where even answering my wife's normal, everyday questions just feels like too much effort. I really hate being like that because she's so supportive, and I want to be a good husband. But it's just hard to care about much of anything during those weeks. 

I try not to let it show too much, but... yeah, it does happen. Does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to be honest with you.

During those periods when you are feeling highly driven and energetic, have you ever felt that your behavior was so extreme or out of control that you required hospitalization to keep yourself safe or to stabilize your mood?

Um, hospitalized? Oh, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, I know I get a bit... intense, like I said, and maybe a little over-enthusiastic about getting things done. But it's never been, you know, dangerous or completely out of control. 

I really try to keep a handle on things, even when my mind is racing with all those ideas. I'd never want things to get so bad that I'd need to be in a hospital. That sounds really scary, honestly. I've always been able to just... well, take a step back, maybe with a little nudge from my wife or my boss, before it ever got to that point. 

I hope that's okay? I just want to reassure you that I'm generally pretty safe, even when I'm running a bit fast. Is that a good sign, that I haven't needed to go to the hospital?
